inventory.name: AccentColor / AccentColorText system colour keywords and accent-color: auto scoped to installed web app contexts

syntax.rationale: #syntax is the 'what changes' heading and its fragment is the declaration surface the page turns on - three existing spellings, not a new property: the system colour keywords AccentColor and AccentColorText, and the auto value of accent-color, each tabulated against the two contexts. The ChromeStatus summary uses the same framing ('AccentColor and AccentColorText CSS keywords, pose a significant fingerprinting vector when exposing the user's system colors widely on the web. As such, they're only available in installed web app contexts. Form controls with accent-color: auto also match this scope with this feature launch.'), and the beta notes are the published form of the same sentence. The 149 restatement of the accent-color: auto half is corroborated by MDN's accent-color data note 'From version 149, to mitigate fingerprinting risks, a fixed value is returned for accent-color: auto unless used within installed web apps on a user's initial profile.'

inputs.rationale: Reduced input surface, documented by the same table: the developer writes one of the three literals and nothing else - the change adds no property, argument, dictionary, media feature or flag - while the browsing context selects the branch. #syntax's 'Regular tab (Chrome 149+)' and 'Installed PWA (Chrome 149+)' columns are that input/context matrix, and the ChromeStatus record describes the feature as a scope restriction on existing values ('This is scoping an existing feature') rather than a new configuration surface.

outputs.rationale: The observable output is the colour each declaration computes to, and #syntax states it per row: in a regular tab 'Returns a fixed default (no longer OS value)' for AccentColor, 'Returns a fixed default' for AccentColorText and 'Browser-chosen default; no OS leak' for accent-color: auto; in an installed PWA 'Returns the user's actual OS accent colour', 'Returns the matching text colour for the accent' and 'OS system accent colour'. Nothing is returned to synchronous script - the change is to the resolved colour value.

errors.rationale: No error surface exists to document: the three spellings already parse, so the restriction introduces no new DOMException, no @supports gate and no unsupported-value or fallback-failure path, and the page documents none.

context.rationale: #at-a-glance fixes the exposure context of the change: 'Shipped in' Chrome 149, Status 'Privacy change — enabled by default', Flag 'None', with the ChromeStatus feature link. The beta notes state the scope boundary the page's lede describes in developer terms: the keywords and accent-color: auto are restricted 'to be only within a web app and initial profile context'.

lifecycle.rationale: #migration is the state-transition table: the same declaration resolved to the OS accent colour before Chrome 149 and resolves to a fixed default from 149 on in a regular tab, while the installed-PWA row states 'Still works — no change in PWA context'. It also carries the migration path for each state (supply your own accent custom property or an explicit 'accent-color: #your-brand').

examples.rationale: #examples is the 'what is an "installed web app" context?' heading and its fragment holds the page's only runnable <pre><code> block: the CSS that sets background-color: AccentColor and color: AccentColorText on a button, annotated 'In Chrome 149+: no longer reads user's system accent' for the regular tab and 'AccentColor / AccentColorText still resolve correctly.' for an installed PWA on the same origin. The same fragment defines the installed web app context the example depends on ('the user has added to their home screen, taskbar, or Start menu ... Regular browser tabs — even on the same origin — are not considered installed app contexts').

compatibility.rationale: #compatibility is the browser-support table and holds the page's per-browser matrix: Chrome '149 — AccentColor restricted to installed PWA scope', Edge '149 (Chromium)', Firefox 'AccentColor always returned a fixed value — no OS leak', Safari 'AccentColor supported; scoping behaviour may differ', attributed to the ChromeStatus browser views. It is the fragment the contract's milestone divergence is recorded against, because MDN's compatibility data for the same two keywords records Chrome and Edge at version_added 150 while recording accent-color: auto as 'From version 149'.

securityPrivacy.rationale: #why-it-exists documents the privacy model the change implements: that AccentColor[Text] 'pose a significant fingerprinting vector when exposing the user's system colors widely on the web', that a script can sample the resolved colour and use it 'as a stable, passively collected fingerprinting signal that persists across clearing cookies, changing IP addresses, or using private browsing', and why installation - 'an explicit, user-consented action' - is the exemption. The ChromeStatus record's security_risks field is null and its privacy_review_status reads 'Pending', so no source-side finding is added beyond the record's own motivation text.

DIVERGENCES FOUND, BOTH SIDES RECORDED, NEITHER ADJUDICATED HERE (disclosure paragraphs and curated-table pin entries are DRAFTED IN THE UNIT REPORT, not written on this page - the implementer owns the sentence and its pin): (1) STATUS/ROLLOUT: this page's #at-a-glance reads 'Shipped in | Chrome 149' and 'Status | Privacy change — enabled by default' (and 'Flag | None'), while the ChromeStatus record reports browsers.chrome.status.text 'Proposed' with is_released false, a desktop milestone of 149, no Android, WebView or iOS milestone, and flag false. (2) MILESTONE FOR THE KEYWORDS: this page's #compatibility table reads Chrome '149 — AccentColor restricted to installed PWA scope' and Edge '149 (Chromium)', while the MDN compatibility data the page's see-also link points at records AccentColor and AccentColorText at version_added 150 in Chrome, 150 in Chrome for Android and 150 in Edge, with the note 'To mitigate fingerprinting risks, a fixed value is returned for AccentColor and AccentColorText unless used within installed web apps on a user's initial profile.' - while recording accent-color: auto's mitigation as 'From version 149' (which agrees with the page). The two sources therefore split the page's single 149 milestone: 149 for accent-color: auto, 150 for the two keywords. (3) SAFARI BROWSER CELL VERSUS THE VIEW THE PAGE CITES FOR THAT TABLE: #compatibility records Safari as 'AccentColor supported; scoping behaviour may differ' under a citation of 'chromestatus browser views', while the record's browsers.safari.view.text is 'No signal' with the note 'In discussion'. UNCORROBORATED, NOT CONTRADICTED (recorded, not resolved): (a) the Firefox cell 'AccentColor always returned a fixed value — no OS leak' is not evidenced by MDN's data (firefox version_added 103 carries no fixed-value note) but IS corroborated by the record's own interop_compat_risks field ('FireFox does not [expose the system accent color completely unscoped]'), and the record's ff view 'Positive' is a standards position on this Chrome change, not a statement of Firefox behaviour - so no divergence is claimed there; (b) the 'initial profile context' qualifier in the record, the beta notes and MDN's data note appears nowhere on the page (the page says 'installed web app contexts' / 'installed PWAs' without it) - an under-listing, not a contradiction; (c) the page's claim that 'the origin must match the app's declared scope in the Web App Manifest' is not documented by the see-also page it is closest to (MDN's Making PWAs installable guide contains no manifest scope rule at all), and no other cited source states it; (d) the page's breaking-change framing for the two keywords ('those styles will no longer reflect the actual system accent in regular browser tabs from Chrome 149') assumes the keywords resolved to the OS accent in regular tabs before the change, while the record's motivation describes AccentColor[Text] as 'planned to only be available in installed web apps' and singles out accent-color: auto as the value that 'uses system accent color everywhere' today - reported as a framing difference only, since the record does not state a hard before-value for the keywords; (e) the Edge cell has no source at all (ChromeStatus carries no Edge data; MDN mirrors Edge to Chrome's value, i.e. 150 per the divergence above). DIMENSIONS: all nine are covered by a resolved fragment; 'errors' is not-applicable with the page-and-record gap stated above rather than invented.
